analysis: Examined the two changed hunks. (1) ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift head lines 204-207: enterAddonHold now also cancels selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task, alongside the existing preloadTasks cancellation. This narrows the T-059 model-load fence gap: a selected-model recovery task could otherwise load a model beside the add-on's VMs. It is a strictly restrictive change with no new input or authorization surface. addonHoldLoadRefusal (head 342-345) still fences loads, and the settle/unload logic is unchanged. Peer authentication (head 61-67), ownedHold isolation, lease/machine-lock handling and restore logic are unchanged. Unverified contract: whether cancelling the recovery task leaves selectedModelRecovery state consistent (no stuck 'attempting' state, and recovery resumes after release). That code is outside the supplied evidence, so it is not a security finding; at most it is an availability question for T-059/A-018. (2) ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift head line ~213: a call to noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command) is added after a successful autopilot eviction. Its implementation is not supplied. It presumably records that the unload was autopilot-initiated so recovery does not reload the model. The call sits inside the loop after the guard on unloadModel, so it runs only on successful unloads and does not change ownership checks (checkAutopilotLoadOwnership) or the consent/control validity gates. I could not verify that the function does not weaken autopilot or recovery semantics, or that it handles the command-cancel path. Cross-file interaction for the next pass: selectedModelRecovery and noteSelectedModelUnloaded implementations, and whether recovery can still load a model during an addon hold through a path other than the cancelled task (e.g. a recovery restart after the cancel). No concrete regression was identified in the supplied code.
